candidates.angle: Unmanifest worship is hard for embodied beings, but this path is open to all
candidates.evidence: For those whose minds cling to the unmanifest, the struggle is greater. The unmanifest path is hard to reach for embodied beings.

candidates.angle: The word yogena, yoga, means a state of evenness, and here it describes how a devotee acts.
The word parah means the highest, and with it Krishna shows where a devotee places their aim.
candidates.evidence: मत्पराः (those devoted to Me as the highest)

angle_en: Total devotion turns every action into worship.

en.intro: Krishna has just said the unmanifest path is hard for those in a body. Now he names a different way, open to anyone.
en.notice: After saying the unmanifest is hard, Krishna names a path where a devotee places every single action at his feet and holds him as the highest aim.
en.next: Krishna then says he quickly lifts those who follow this path out of the ocean of mortal existence, O Partha.
en.angle_en: Krishna names a path open to all
en.angle_hi: कृष्ण सभी के लिए एक मार्ग बताते हैं
en.meaning: But those who surrender all actions to Me, take Me as their highest aim, and worship Me with single-pointed devotion, meditating on Me alone.

hi.intro: कृष्ण ने अभी कहा कि शरीर वालों के लिए अव्यक्त का मार्ग कठिन है। अब वे एक ऐसा मार्ग बताते हैं जो सबके लिए खुला है।
hi.meaning: परन्तु जो मेरी शरण में होकर, मुझे ही सर्वोच्च मानकर, अनन्य योग से मेरा ही ध्यान करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं।
hi.notice: अव्यक्त को कठिन बताने के बाद, कृष्ण ऐसे भक्त का वर्णन करते हैं जो हर कर्म उन्हें सौंप देता है और उन्हें ही अपना सर्वोच्च लक्ष्य मानता है।
hi.next: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि वे ऐसे लोगों को शीघ्र ही मृत्यु के सागर से पार करा देते हैं, हे पार्थ।

en.intro: Krishna has just said the unmanifest path is hard for those in a body. Now he names a different way, open to anyone.
en.body: But those who surrender all actions to Me, take Me as their highest aim, and worship Me with single-pointed devotion, meditating on Me alone. After saying the unmanifest is hard, Krishna names a path where a devotee places every single action at his feet and holds him as the highest aim. Krishna then says he quickly lifts those who follow this path out of the ocean of mortal existence, O Partha.

hi.intro: कृष्ण ने अभी कहा कि शरीर वालों के लिए अव्यक्त का मार्ग कठिन है। अब वे एक ऐसा मार्ग बताते हैं जो सबके लिए खुला है।
hi.body: परन्तु जो मेरी शरण में होकर, मुझे ही सर्वोच्च मानकर, अनन्य योग से मेरा ही ध्यान करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं। अव्यक्त को कठिन बताने के बाद, कृष्ण ऐसे भक्त का वर्णन करते हैं जो हर कर्म उन्हें सौंप देता है और उन्हें ही अपना सर्वोच्च लक्ष्य मानता है। कृष्ण कहते हैं कि वे ऐसे लोगों को शीघ्र ही मृत्यु के सागर से पार करा देते हैं, हे पार्थ।

issues: unsupported: "कृष्ण ने अभी कहा कि शरीर वालों के लिए अव्यक्त का मार्ग कठिन है। अब वे एक ऐसा मार्ग बताते हैं जो सबके लिए खुला है।" (The Hindi intro adds the unsupported claim that this path is 'open to everyone' (सबके लिए खुला है). The Sanskrit verse specifically describes those who are 'matparah' (taking Me as the highest aim), indicating a specific type of devotee, not a universal path open to anyone regardless of devotion.)

meaning_changed: "परन्तु जो मेरी शरण में होकर, मुझे ही सर्वोच्च मानकर, अनन्य योग से मेरा ही ध्यान करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं।" (The Hindi meaning drops the explicit surrender of all actions ('sarvani karmani mayi samnyasya'), which is a core component of the Sanskrit verse. It replaces it with a more general 'sharan' (taking refuge), softening the specific instruction of offering all actions.)

meaning_changed: "परन्तु जो सभी कर्मों को मेरे अर्पण करके, मुझे ही सर्वोच्च मानकर, अनन्य योग से मेरा ही ध्यान करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं।" (The Hindi translation adds the phrase 'सर्वोच्च मानकर' (considering as the highest) which is not present in the source text or its standard word-by-word meanings. The source specifies 'मत्पराः' (those devoted to Me as the highest), which implies being the ultimate goal, but 'सर्वोच्च मानकर' is an interpretive addition not found in the Sanskrit word meanings provided.)

unsupported: "कृष्ण ने अभी कहा कि शरीर वालों के लिए अव्यक्त का मार्ग कठिन है। अब वे उन भक्तों का वर्णन करते हैं जो हर कर्म उन्हें सौंप देते हैं।" (The intro states that Krishna 'just said' the unmanifest path is hard for embodied beings, implying it was the immediately preceding statement. However, in the actual script, the previous verse (5) is quoted as 'For those whose minds cling to the unmanifest...' but the intro presents it as a direct, immediate quote from Krishna in the narrative flow, which is an unsupported narrative framing.)

unsupported: "अव्यक्त को कठिन बताने के बाद, कृष्ण ऐसे भक्त का वर्णन करते हैं जो हर कर्म उन्हें सौंप देता है और उन्हें ही अपना सर्वोच्च लक्ष्य मानता है।" (The Hindi notice claims that Krishna describes a devotee 'after saying the unmanifest is hard'. However, the source verse (6) itself does not explicitly state 'after saying the unmanifest is hard' within its own text. It simply describes the devotees. The 'after' part is a narrative sequencing detail from the intro, not a factual claim within the verse itself, but the notice frames it as if the verse contains this temporal marker, making it an unsupported narrative detail.)
